checker.capture: each command's stdout+stderr to a file, exit code via $? appended; time / peak RSS from /usr/bin/time -f '%e %M' on the honest run

digest_definitions.cp_verify_sha256: sha256sum bin/cp_verify after verifier/build.sh (our binary; builds may differ by toolchain)
digest_definitions.verifier_source_digest: the build= field cp_verify prints: verifier/build.sh (line 311) hashes the verifier sources and headers -- not build.sh itself, the compiler or its flags; equal values mean the same sources

checker.isolation: unprivileged user, no network, read-only system, 2.2 GB memory cap
checker.party: invinoveritas: not the producer (Anthropic); a member of the Trustless-AI working group (github.com/trustless-ai), so not independent of its members' own checks; checked on its own machine

procedure.flipped_byte: copy example.proof, XOR byte 2072650 (0-based) with 0x01, run the honest command on the copy
procedure.honest: cd examples/accepted-proof && ../../bin/cp_verify config ivk example.req example.y example.proof -id "$(cat ID.txt)"
procedure.wrong_id: run the honest command with -id 09a5a2bc7a469b40df73dedf40abeb740671e8ae8077738bd3743897aeb22183 (first hex digit 7 -> 0)

covers: this proof file verifies under cp_verify at this commit for this commitment ID, on a machine operated by the party named in checker (an attestation by that party; the commands and digests here let anyone repeat it)
the check refuses the two altered inputs tried here: this one byte-flipped copy of the proof (sha256 given) and this one wrong commitment ID -- not a claim about all alterations
does_not_cover: anything about a served or real model (the example uses synthetic weights)
the Lean proof's coverage of cp_verify (the Lean proof covers FlashProve's Lean verifier, as the authors state)
where the input came from (input provenance)
whether any action taken on the output was authorised (decision authorisation)
that what ran in production is what was proven (execution binding)
the full-size Maverick-shape proof (not run here)
